This action slows the absorption of carbohydrates, helping to control blood glucose levels.

The key mechanism of miglitol involves inhibiting the enzyme alpha-glucosidase, which relies on the cleavage of glycosidic bonds in carbohydrates. By inhibiting this enzyme, miglitol prevents the breakdown of polysaccharides and oligosaccharides into monosaccharides, thereby reducing the postprandial glucose spike.
